takeaway: Thoracic aorta branches: bronchial, pericardial, posterior intercostal, superior phrenic, oesophageal, mediastinal and subcostal arteries. Lumbar and inferior phrenic arteries come from the abdominal aorta.

lines.text: The thoracic aorta is the thoracic part of the descending aorta. Which artery is its direct branch?
Its branches include the bronchial and pericardial arteries,
the posterior intercostal and superior phrenic arteries,
and the subcostal arteries. There is our answer.
lines.say: (laugh) and the subcostal arteries. There is our answer.

lines.text: The lumbar and inferior phrenic arteries are paired branches of the abdominal aorta.
The inferior phrenic arteries may even arise from the coeliac trunk.
So the direct branch of the thoracic aorta is the subcostal artery.
